name: Megan Fischer

five_sec.what_is_it: Something that picks dinners and puts the groceries in your Instacart or Walmart cart, and texts your family to vote, which is cute.
five_sec.who_for: Families with older kids who can text back. Mine are 2 and 4 months, so, my husband votes I guess.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Dinner, handled.' is exactly what I want to hear, but there's no picture of any food or any family on the first screen, just a lot of words.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It literally says 'We don't deliver food.' So wait, I still have to cook and get the groceries? Okay but the cart part means Instacart brings it.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Not much. The Kroger cart is only on the paid Family plan and Kroger pickup is what I actually use. And it's not a box, so I still have to cook every night.
full_page.whats_missing: Cost per serving (I had to do the math: about $3.20). Kroger cart on the free plan.

DD.quote: $64 for five dinners for four and nothing over 35 minutes, that's like $3 a serving, way under my EveryPlate math, and it goes in my Kroger cart?

five_sec.what_is_it: An app that just tells you what's for dinner before you ask.
five_sec.trust_why: 90,000 families and the phone picture looks really polished.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's a menu in an app with little notifications, no box.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Went to pricing and it's $25 a month for the normal one and they count your messages. The meal page said a 1-month free trial, so I'm confused which is true. Also no Kroger, just Instacart, Walmart, Amazon Fresh.
full_page.whats_missing: A cost per meal, Kroger, one clear price.

OL.quote: 'The mental load of dinner, lifted' got me at 3 a.m., then the pricing page said $25 a month and they count messages.

five_sec.what_is_it: An app for saving recipes and making meal plans and lists.
five_sec.who_for: Planner people. Pinterest girls with time.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Saving recipes from Pinterest is fun, but I'd still have to make the plan. 'Your recipes, your schedule, your plan' is the opposite of what I need right now.
full_page.whats_missing: Someone choosing the dinners for me.

PTE.quote: Saving Pinterest recipes is cute, but 'your recipes, your schedule, your plan' is the exact thing I can't do with a newborn.

five_sec.what_is_it: HelloFresh, meal kits, basically fancier EveryPlate.
five_sec.who_for: People with more money than us on maternity leave pay.
five_sec.trust_why: I know the brand. The mystery box game is fun for a second, then it's obviously a sales thing.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Boxes, food bowls, it's a meal kit.

full_page.what_stopped_me: No price unless I type my zip, and I already know it's more than EveryPlate. Fine print says the free meals count is based on a 4-person 5-recipe plan.
full_page.whats_missing: A price per meal on the page.

HF.quote: Okay the open-a-box thing got me for a sec, but I'd have to type my zip to see a price and I know it's more than EveryPlate.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal plans app, mom and little girl in the video.
five_sec.who_for: Moms with little kids, like me.
five_sec.next_step: Scroll for kid stuff and the price.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'Choose Your Meals', phone with a checklist.

full_page.what_stopped_me: I scrolled the whole page and couldn't find what it costs. There's a pop-up for my email though.

EM.quote: Kid Friendly plan and it sends to Kroger, nice, but I scrolled the whole thing at 3 a.m. and never found what it costs.

dd_offer.why: I get no card, but the Kroger cart is in the Family part, so I wasn't sure if Kroger stops working after two weeks.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: After two weeks the texting and the Kroger cart go away unless I pay $4.99, and I keep the free planner with Instacart and Walmart.

head_to_head.reason: It picks the dinners, shows what the week costs, and it's cheaper per serving than EveryPlate.

EM.reason: DinnerDrop shows a price and a weekly grocery total; eMeals shows neither.

PTE.reason: DinnerDrop plans for me; Plan to Eat makes me plan.

OL.reason: Ollie feels nicer but $25 a month with counted messages is a lot; DinnerDrop is free or $4.99.

HF.reason: Way cheaper, even if I have to cook from the store.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page sample week: put the cost per serving next to the $64 total (about $3.20 a serving), so I can compare it to EveryPlate's $4.99 without doing math at 3 a.m.
